Maria: Morning — noticed a noisy alert from nightly perf CI (small-batch p95). Baseline ~420ms -> last run 820ms on gpu-x. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/perf/abcd :eyes:
Maria: artifacts: http://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/job/6872, logs attached. Can someone pick this up?
ci-bot: nightly-perf-ci #6872 finished with status: FAILED (regression detected). Artifacts: http://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/job/6872
Ryan: I'll take a look, starting a bisect now. @Samir do you know of any infra/runtime changes in the last 24h? :thumbsup:
Samir: Not from infra side in prod, but there was a library bump in the runtime image: cupy 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 in PR #5123 yesterday. Could be relevant.
Samir: Suggest running: `./scripts/run_smallbatch.sh --model llama-7b-quant --commit-range 4a1b2c..e9f0d1 --repeat 30` locally to repro.
Olivia: Traces from the run show longer queue/warmup time. Snapshot: `queue_ms`: 12 -> 180, `kernel_launch_ms`: +30ms variance. Might be scheduling/backpressure.
Ben: Uploading flamegraph: http://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/job/6872/flamegraph.svg. Grepped logs for "kernel launch" and saw some back-to-back spikes. `grep -n "kernel launch" perf.log | tail -n 20`
Ben: Hypothesis: small-batch path is more sensitive to a change in continuous-batching merge policy or a kernel change in cupy.
Maria: Added candidate PR that modified batching heuristics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5119. Also put a pinned link to nightly run: http://dash.redwood.internal/perf/compare/4a1b2c..e9f0d1
Ryan: Running bisect now (starting commits 4a1b2c..e9f0d1). Will report back in ~90m. If I can repro locally I'll try a quick revert. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ci-bot: bisect job #6873 started (runner: perf-bisect-3). Logs streaming: http://ci.redwood/internal/logs/6873
Samir: If bisect narrows to runtime, can we get a kernel/scheduler trace from the failing node? `sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` then grab the perf data from the artifact store.
Olivia: Also check node load and container throttling, saw a noisy neighbor in a different run earlier tonight.
Maria: Good points. If bisect points at the cupy bump or PR #5119 I'll open an urgent rollback. Otherwise if it's infra, pinging @eng-sre-oncall to collect node-level traces and check any kube-scheduler changes.
eng-sre-oncall: Acknowledged, will start collecting node traces and kube events for the time window of the failing run.
Ryan: First bisect result: narrowed to range, suspecting commit `e3f9a2` which touches batching and kernel dispatch. Running focused repro on dedicated instance now.
Ben: If you need a repro script, use: `python experiments/repro_smallbatch.py --commit e3f9a2 --iters 100 --batch-size 4` — I used a variant earlier that reproduced the 2x p95.
Maria: Thanks — keeping this thread updated. If anyone finds a quick mitigation (config toggle or revert) drop it here and we'll coordinate a roll. :thumbsup:
Ryan: Will post full bisect log to the artifacts when done.
ci-bot: bisect job #6873 completed (status: SUCCESS). Result: probable culprit commit e3f9a2. Artifacts: http://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/job/6873/bisect-report.json
Maria: Great, thanks. @eng-sre-oncall please correlate node traces with the bisect window. If confirmed, I'll cut a rollback PR for the batching change.
eng-sre-oncall: On it, will update in 30m.
